free_tier.stated: 50 GB per public project, 5 GB per private project, 5 GB per file. But 'Each Component on a project has its own 5GB/50GB storage limit' and, crucially, 'Currently, there is no applied overall cap on the amount of OSF Storage per user.' Component trees are unbounded, so this is per-unit quota, not per-account.

egress.terms: Unmetered; downloads served from OSF Storage (US/Canada/Germany/Australia regions)

record.tooling: OSF open API v2 (api.osf.io/v2, JSON:API: nodes, files, waterbutler); official osfclient Python package; OSF is the canonical 'component = free bucket' multiplier
record.chaining: 50 GB x unlimited components x (optionally) unlimited projects. A project can nest components, each with its own 50 GB, and there is no overall per-user cap. So the structure is the same per-record multiplier as Zenodo but with a smaller unit (50 GB) and a much lower per-file ceiling (5 GB).
record.limits_note: 5 GB per file is the hard limit. Worse than Zenodo's 50 GB and worse than Harvard's 2.5 GB only in being middling. 5 GB applies to private projects, so working storage is the expensive tier here; 50 GB requires making the project public.

identity_cost.detail: inferred from the category 'academic'; the source record states no identity cost, so this is a class assumption, not evidence

record.reliability_note: OSF is mid-'Project Transition' per its own help banner, which is a structural-change risk for a long-lived archive. Storage is regional and selectable only at project creation and cannot be moved afterwards.
